title: God's commandments are not burdensome
source_text: XI. Itaque jure merito Joannes epist. primae cap. quinto affirmat mandata Dei non esse gravia. Etenim, praeterquam quod nihil a nobis exigunt quod naturae & rationi valde consentaneum, & nobis maxime conducibile non sit, Deus etiam suis vires sufficit, per quas mandata ejus effecta dare possint, & per gratiam suam praestat, ut illa pii & fideles observent.
pass_a_gloss: XI. And so rightly does John in the first epistle chap. five affirm that the commandments of God are not heavy. For, besides the fact that they demand nothing from us which is not very agreeable to nature & reason, & most advantageous to us, God also supplies strength to his own, through which they can carry out his commandments, & through his grace brings it about, that the godly & faithful observe them.
pass_b_english: Thesis XI. John is therefore right to say, in the fifth chapter of his first epistle, that God's commandments are not burdensome. They require nothing of us that is not in close accord with nature and reason and very much to our good.
Besides this, God gives his own people the strength to carry out his commandments, and by his grace he ensures that the devout and faithful keep them.

lemmas.gloss: that the commandments of God are not heavy

choices.why: Scripture's phrase for the obedience of believers, kept distinct from perfect fulfilment of the law.
